data.title: Zlatý kôň – a drawing of the Púchov-culture fortlet by Peter Bros
data.excerpt: Our collaborator Peter Bros has drawn an artistic visualisation of the Celtic (Púchov-culture) fortlet of Zlatý kôň, whose remains can be seen above the village of Prosné. The narrow, elongated site followed a mountain ridge and probably served as a refuge for the people of the surrounding settlements in times of danger.

children.text: Our collaborator Peter Bros has drawn this artistic visualisation of the Celtic

, whose remains can be seen above the village of Prosné. In the rear part of the fortlet it can be seen that the people of the Púchov culture built a timber-and-earth rampart with a wooden palisade here, while in the front part the steep slope meant that it was enough to set up a wooden fence and no rampart had to be built. The fortlet probably served as a refuge for the inhabitants of the surrounding settlements at times when they were threatened by Germanic peoples or other enemies. It had a narrow, elongated shape and followed the mountain ridge.

Peter drew the fortlet from a greater distance than Antonín Lacko did, so that people can form a better idea of what the whole fortlet may have looked like. If it was indeed a refuge, we have to allow for the possibility that the quality of the defences did not reach the level we are used to at the more important oppida, for example. Between the individual posts set into the ground there need not always, and not all the way round the fortlet, have been thick beams or planks; wattling of branches or thinner trees can also be assumed.
